title: Benchmark CAD/BIM performance, scalability, and operational robustness
objective: Determine whether the candidate CAD/BIM stack (FreeCAD 1.1.3 / OpenCascade, IfcOpenShell 0.8.5, behind the frozen adapter boundary) is operationally viable for representative ConstructionOS workloads by measuring performance, memory behavior, scalability, determinism, failure recovery and resource isolation across at least three fixture scales, separating engine performance from Offisos adapter/translation overhead, and producing evidence for the licensing/composition and implementation-path decision. This research gate does not establish final production thresholds (none are numerically defined in compatibility-matrix.md); it produces the raw, reproducible evidence for deciding whether future thresholds are realistic and whether the candidate remains viable behind the frozen adapter boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible benchmark harness exists for the scoped operations (application start/load; model open/import; geometry preparation; selection/query; parametric edit/recompute; boolean/geometry operations; IFC import/export; semantic extraction; quantity extraction; controlled save/reopen).

At least three fixture scales are exercised with documented characteristics (small architectural, medium construction, larger stress representative of anticipated professional use, plus IFC fixtures with increasing entity/geometry counts).
Import/export, recompute, semantic extraction and quantity extraction have measured timings.
Memory/resource behavior (peak RSS, file sizes, entity counts) is recorded for representative workloads.
Repeated-run variance and nondeterminism are measured or explicitly shown to be absent for deterministic operations (medians and distributions, not only best-case samples).
At least one failure/recovery scenario is exercised and documented (malformed fixtures, failed-operation recovery, cancellation/interruption, large-operation timeout, corruption/data-loss detection).
Evidence identifies any workload where the candidate exceeds available resources or becomes materially unstable.

Results identify concrete operational constraints needed by the adapter/worker boundary (process/thread isolation requirements, worker/native-worker execution, resource limits protecting the modular monolith).
Engine performance is separated from Offisos adapter/translation overhead in the measurements.
Recommendation is one of: (a) candidate remains operationally viable; (b) viable with explicit constraints; (c) rejected; (d) architecture change request required.
non_goals: No change to the frozen architecture (v1.1).
No claim that benchmark results generalize to every future model size.
No acceptance based solely on a single fast demo.
No final licensing/composition decision (separate downstream gate).

Measurement environments differ between the local evidence run and CI (GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners): the evidence states clearly where measurements are not comparable because of different execution environments; both environments run the identical pinned toolchain and identical fixtures, and the benchmark records an environment snapshot with every run.

FreeCAD GUI-dependent operations (rendering/view pipelines) are not measurable headless; geometry preparation is measured via the console-mode recompute/ tessellation paths and this limitation is recorded honestly rather than approximated.

Wall-clock timing assertions use distributional/regression bounds (orderings, ratios, coarse ceilings) rather than absolute time thresholds, because absolute thresholds are not defined by the compatibility matrix and hardware differs across environments.
evidence_requirements: Exact engine/library versions, hardware, OS, runtime and benchmark configuration recorded for every run (environment snapshot).
Fixtures, scripts and raw measurement output stored reproducibly in the repository under research/cad-005/.
Medians and distributions for repeated operations where meaningful, not only best-case samples.
Failures and resource exhaustion recorded rather than omitted.
Engine time separated from Offisos adapter/translation overhead in the measurements.
Representative workloads compared across at least three fixture scales.
Clear statement where measurements are not comparable because of different execution environments.

evidence.description: Local full evidence run of the RESEARCH-CAD-005 benchmark (research/cad-005/evidence/run-001): 83 pass / 0 fail / 0 unknown across ten modules — fixture tiers, IFC engine operations (open/export/query with engine-vs-adapter split), OCCT booleans/tessellation/STEP-IO incl. the multi-tool boolean scaling cliff, FreeCAD document lifecycle in process-isolated FreeCADCmd (cold start 82-114ms, open/edit/recompute/save/reopen at 40/240/840-object tiers with child peak RSS), semantic+quantity extraction scaling, repeated-run variance (CV 4.1%/1.9%/0.9%) and result determinism, robustness (malformed input, typed failures, corruption, durable-write), cancellation (in-process non-preemptability proof, subprocess cancel/timeout, recovery), isolation (parent never imports FreeCAD, thread non-parallelism, resource exhaustion in both modes), and the adapter/worker constraint synthesis with the recommendation (b) viable with explicit constraints. Environment snapshot attached (2-core Xeon, pinned ifcopenshell 0.8.5 / OCCT 7.8.1.1 / FreeCAD 1.1.3).
